- FOMC stance: Rates held at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent; labor market strong, inflation below 2 percent, and uncertainties elevated; guidance to “act as appropriate.”
- SLOOS cross-check: Banks reported tighter standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and tighter other terms; weaker demand for construction/land development, HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans; demand roughly unchanged for auto and subprime mortgages.
- Implications: Tighter credit availability and softer loan demand point to headwinds for business fixed investment and consumer spending, reinforcing the FOMC’s caution and dovish tilt despite solid employment. Macro remains modestly positive, but SLOOS nudges the outlook more cautious than a purely macro read.
